rationale: hammernik_2017-claude-agentic: vn_T=5, vn_n_filters=16, vn_kernel=11, vn_n_bumps=31, vn_x_range=2.0, vn_lambda_init=0.0023, epochs=19, batch_size=2, lr=0.0003, grad_clip=1.0, train_n=200, val_n=214, max_train_s=1100, seed=42, rationale=hammernik_2017 iter-6 (search-20260619-01, corrected 214-slice/321px-FOV metric). ONE KNOB: lr 5e-4 -> 3e-4 (0.6x). BASE_ITER=5 (the NEW BEST + FIRST above-baseline point: SSIM 0.8114, hr 0.0319, ep19/bs2/lr5e-4). All else held at iter-5 (vn_T=5, vn_n_filters=16, vn_kernel=11, vn_n_bumps=31, vn_x_range=2.0, vn_lambda_init=0.0023, epochs=19, batch_size=2, grad_clip=1.0, train_n=200, val_n=214, max_train_s=1100, seed=42). TRAJECTORY (corrected metric): iter-1 OOM(bs4); iter-2 0.8012 hr0; iter-3 0.7932 hr0 (lambda 0.0023->0.05 REGRESSED); iter-4 0.7828 hr0 (n_filters 16->4 REGRESSED); iter-5 0.8114 hr0.0319 KEEP (epochs 14->19, FIRST above the 0.84-ish LD-FBP floor -- under-training diagnosis CONFIRMED, the epochs lever WORKS). LIMITER (box2): the VN is still under-trained toward its proven ep38 convergence basin (the discarded boundary-slice sweep climbed SSIM 0.876->0.9484 over ep8->38), BUT ep19 is WALL-PINNED: iter-5 train was 1071.6s at 56.4s/epoch, elapsed 1166.5s; ONE more epoch = 1128s train + ~95s score(214) = ~1223s > the HARD 1200s budget, so epochs CANNOT go up. The solver uses a PLAIN Adam with NO lr scheduler and consumes no lr_decay/cosine/weight_decay knob (verified by grep) and I may NOT edit the shared solver file -- so an lr-decay schedule is unavailable as a cfg knob. The decisive EVIDENCE for the lever: the iter-5 loss curve CONVERGED numerically by ep11 (~8e-7) yet SSIM is still far below the proven 0.9484 -- loss-convergence != SSIM-convergence for this VN -- AND there is an ep18 INSTABILITY BLIP (loss spiked 8.2e-7 -> 2.5e-6 then recovered to 7.9e-7 at ep19), direct evidence the late-training trajectory is BOUNCING near its basin at lr=5e-4 rather than settling. The budget cannot buy more epochs, so the lever must improve convergence QUALITY within the fixed 19 epochs. ONE KNOB CHOICE (box3): lr 5e-4->3e-4 shrinks every late-training step, damping the ep18-style bounce so the net settles into a better basin instead of overshooting it -- the finer-convergence/stable-late-training lever the protocol prescribes, and exactly the iter-5 pre-registered falsifier path (iter-5: if val_ssim<=0.84 at 19 epochs, iter-6 must lower lr). It is BUDGET-NEUTRAL (lr is a scalar -- identical per-step compute), unlike batch_size which carries an unsized wall-cost risk. lr is held DOWN not up because the campaign record says lr5e-4 optimal and 8e-4 WORSE for the VN family (5e-4 vs 3e-4 is untested). HYPOTHESIS (box4): if lr->3e-4, the late steps shrink and the ep18 instability is damped so the net settles into a better basin -> predict val_ssim rises above 0.8114 (hr > 0.0319), targeting ~0.82-0.83 / hr ~0.04-0.06. FALSIFIER: if val_ssim <= 0.8114 (hr <= 0.0319), lower lr starves the under-trained net of progress more than it stabilizes it -> the bs=2/19-epoch budget is convergence-bounded and iter-7 must trade gradient STEPS (batch_size 2->1 doubles optimizer steps/epoch at ~the same per-epoch wall, attacking the proven step-count limiter directly) -- the only remaining within-budget step-count lever once lr is shown not to help. BUDGET (box5, HARD 1200s train+score; sbatch --time=00:30:00): lr is a scalar, ZERO change to per-step compute, so cost == iter-5: 56.4s/epoch x 19 = 1071.6s train + ~95s score(214)+figure = ~1166s predicted elapsed < 1200s; max_train_s=1100 backstop trips before the figure, well under the 1800s SLURM kill. MEMORY-SAFE: identical footprint to iter-5 -- batch_size=2 KEPT (the OOM-safe value; bs=4 OOMed the 16GB RTX5000 in the _rho_prime RBF-bump loop at iter-1), N_k=16, 31-bump RBF across 5 unrolled steps within 16 GB. grad_clip=1.0 retained (VN-family NaN-skip stability).
